name: Zone Planner
description: Designates zone types (residential, commercial, industrial, or any configured set) onto regions of an existing tile grid, and owns the growth rules that decide whether a zoned cell develops. Growth is evaluated per cell against demand pressure and service coverage, so a zone designation is a promise of intent, not a building — nothing appears until the rules say the land is worth developing. This component deliberately does not place structures: world.environment_builder and presentation.object_placer own the act of putting geometry in the world, and zone_planner only tells them where development is wanted. It also does not simulate the people who fill the zones — that is world.citizen_agent_sim, which listens for zone designations to decide where citizens can live and work. The planner's boundary is land-use state and growth eligibility; everything visual and everything agentic lives downstream.

inputs.name: zoneTypes
inputs.description: The zoning palette: ids like residential/commercial/industrial, each with its own growth rules. Data-driven so a farming sim can ship crop/pasture instead of R/C/I without a schema change.

inputs.name: growthTickSeconds
inputs.description: How often growth eligibility is re-evaluated per zoned cell. Growth on every frame is wasted work in a genre where nothing meaningful changes in under a second.

inputs.name: dezoneRefundFraction
inputs.description: Fraction of development value returned when the player clears a developed zone. 0 makes bulldozing a pure loss, which is the classic genre pressure; higher values soften the sim for casual play.

inputs.name: maxZoneBrushSize
inputs.description: Largest single-stroke paint area in tiles. Exists to keep one misclick from rezoning a city, and to give higher tiers a meaningful unlock.

outputs.name: zonedCells
outputs.description: Map of cell coordinates to zone assignment, including development state (vacant, growing, developed).

outputs.name: growthEligibility
outputs.description: Per-cell pass/fail growth evaluation with reasons, so advisory UI can explain 'why won't this area develop' instead of leaving the player guessing.
